limitations: The audit can assess only the supplied 1254 x 1254 rendered sheet and its bound metadata.
Rear construction, underside, dimensions, topology, UVs, collision and Roblox runtime performance are not observable.
A missing proof is reported as UNKNOWN or a limitation, never converted into a visual failure.

strengthsToPreserve: Wide, low and grounded barricade read with two outer load-bearing feet.
Three large panel rhythm inside a continuous dark standardized frame.
Restrained deep-slate, bone-sand, copper and mint palette with strong value separation.
Chunky bevel language, calm primary planes and clean neutral presentation.
Immediate friendly defensive-prop readability with no generated text.

findings.problem: The sheet contains four alternative objects, not four views of one frozen object.
findings.evidence: Brace direction, frame caps, post construction, panel proportions and foot details change between quadrants.
findings.correction: Use one object and one state per board; allow only camera or diagnostic rendering mode to change.

findings.problem: The four exploration candidates are not genuinely different silhouettes.
findings.evidence: All candidates retain the same rectangular frame, three-panel rhythm and feet; most variation is limited to copper-brace placement and trim.
findings.correction: Require each exploration candidate to change at least two primary-mass or negative-space decisions; reject brace-only variation.

findings.problem: No candidate or bounded image region is selected as the continuing object identity.
findings.evidence: The review binds the entire sheet and contains no selected quadrant, crop or preserve rule.
findings.correction: Start the state campaign from one closed canon construction and require explicit preserve rules before acceptance.

findings.problem: The sheet provides no mechanically useful rear view.
findings.evidence: Every quadrant is a front or near-front three-quarter presentation.
findings.correction: Require a three-quarter rear view of the exact hero construction, including the protected player-side repair socket.

findings.problem: There is no black-silhouette proof.
findings.evidence: All quadrants use shaded materials and internal detail.
findings.correction: Require a solid black silhouette whose outer contour matches the hero view.

findings.problem: There is no elevated Roblox mobile gameplay-camera proof.
findings.evidence: All candidates use a studio concept-art camera at a similar distance.
findings.correction: Require one elevated mobile gameplay view in every state-definition board.

findings.problem: Intact, damaged and critical states are not separately defined or verifiable.
findings.evidence: The request metadata names three states, but the output contract asks for four silhouettes and the image shows no state lineage.
findings.correction: Generate one independent board per object state and never mix states in one image.

findings.problem: Damage-state continuity cannot be proven from this result.
findings.evidence: No accepted intact construction is hash-bound as the parent of damaged, and no damaged construction is parent of critical.
findings.correction: Hash-bind damaged to accepted intact and critical to accepted damaged; transform named components only.

findings.problem: Threat-facing front and player-safe rear are visually ambiguous.
findings.evidence: The same armor presentation and mint cue appear on the presented face, while no safe service face is shown.
findings.correction: Make front a continuous threat armor face and rear a calmer service face with the protected interaction socket.

findings.problem: The mint friendly interaction cue is exposed on the threat-facing presentation side.
findings.evidence: A bright cyan or mint lamp is visible on the right post in every candidate.
findings.correction: Keep mint emission local to the protected rear repair socket and absent from the threat-facing armor.

findings.problem: The copper brace often reads as a decorative diagonal stripe instead of a load-bearing repair.
findings.evidence: Several brace ends terminate on panel faces or ornamental plates without a visible structural load path.
findings.correction: Terminate the single repair brace at two plausible frame or load-bearing joints and expose its causal weak-span purpose.

findings.problem: Salvaged Frontier is not expressed through a specific survival history.
findings.evidence: The objects read mainly as clean standardized toy-defense barriers with generic scratches and an added copper bar.
findings.correction: Show one causal reinforcement and one bounded replacement history while keeping the standardized chassis dominant.

findings.problem: Industrial Toy Defense dominates instead of acting only as readability discipline.
findings.evidence: Uniform modular framing, polished beveled panels and decorative hardware carry more identity than frontier repair history.
findings.correction: Preserve toy-like readability but make authored adaptation, material replacement and repair causality own the world identity.

findings.problem: Bone-sand panels read as stone, concrete, parchment or ceramic slabs rather than reclaimed manufactured composite.
findings.evidence: The warm panels use mottled mineral-like texture, chipped slab edges and little manufactured layer or fastening evidence.
findings.correction: Use controlled composite grain, formed edges, layered construction and functional fasteners; forbid mineral or parchment reading.

findings.problem: The copper reinforcement looks too clean, homogeneous and ornamental for an older maintained field repair.
findings.evidence: Its saturation and finish are uniform, with little contact wear or attachment-specific history.
findings.correction: Keep copper bounded but add functional contact wear, fastening logic and restrained value variation at real joints.

findings.problem: Surface distress is generic and distributed too uniformly.
findings.evidence: Small scratches and chips appear across most dark-frame surfaces without strong directional or contact logic.
findings.correction: Concentrate wear at feet, exposed corners, fasteners and contact paths; preserve calm planes elsewhere.

findings.problem: Authored asymmetry is weak or ornamental rather than structural.
findings.evidence: The primary frame, panel rhythm and feet remain highly symmetrical; asymmetry is mostly a movable brace or small cap.
findings.correction: Keep the chassis standardized but place the approved asymmetry in one causal replacement or repair zone.

findings.problem: A triangular pseudo-logo or assembly emblem appears on the lower-left candidate.
findings.evidence: The upper copper plate contains a centered triangular symbol-like construction unrelated to a visible joint.
findings.correction: Remove standalone emblems and permit tertiary geometry only where it explains a real joint or fastener.

findings.problem: Component topology and attachment language drift across quadrants.
findings.evidence: Brace count and shape, top caps, corner posts, feet and panel outlines are not identical between the four candidates.
findings.correction: Apply a cross-view identity lock to counts, positions, joints, wear, material assignments and state topology.

findings.problem: Armor-panel mounting and destructibility are not visually explained.
findings.evidence: Panels appear seated in frames, but their clamps, hinges, sacrificial mounts or intended failure path are inconsistent or absent.
findings.correction: Define stable panel mounts and one declared weak span so damage operations remain mechanically legible.

findings.problem: The required 8 x 4 x 2 stud dimensions and pivot are not proven.
findings.evidence: The sheet has no scale reference, orthographic dimension overlay or geometry measurement.
findings.correction: Treat dimensions as UNKNOWN until reconstructed geometry passes numeric validation; never infer them from this image.

findings.problem: Recognition and state readability at 60 studs are unproven.
findings.evidence: No distance-render or in-game camera sample is present.
findings.correction: Require mobile-distance and Roblox-context validation after state boards and during 3D QA.

findings.problem: Visual repetition and performance at 30 simultaneous barricades are unproven.
findings.evidence: The image contains isolated candidates only, not one repeated asset in Roblox.
findings.correction: Defer PASS until the 3D asset is tested at 1, 30 and stress quantity with shared MeshIds and measured budgets.

findings.problem: Rear, underside, collision, topology, UVs and hidden mechanisms cannot be validated.
findings.evidence: Only shaded front-biased pixels are supplied; the result explicitly has no geometry authority.
findings.correction: Keep these gates UNKNOWN until Blender and Roblox validators supply direct evidence.

findings.problem: Use of the required gpt-image-2 model is not confirmed.
findings.evidence: result.json records modelName as null and modelNameEvidence as NOT_CONFIRMED.
findings.correction: Require the operator attestation that gpt-image-2 was visibly selected before import.

findings.problem: The review accepted a PRECANONICAL_CANDIDATE while three of five assessment dimensions were UNKNOWN.
findings.evidence: visualHierarchy, internalCoherence and stateCoherence are UNKNOWN in review.json.
findings.correction: Require all five assessment dimensions to be PASS for candidate or human-selected acceptance.

findings.problem: The accepted review records no preserve rule.
findings.evidence: review.json contains an empty preserve array.
findings.correction: Require at least one explicit preserve rule before candidate or human-selected acceptance.

findings.problem: The review records no correction despite unresolved visual and evidence gaps.
findings.evidence: review.json contains an empty correct array while three assessments remain UNKNOWN.
findings.correction: Require at least one correction for REVISION_REQUIRED or REJECTED decisions and expose the requirement in the UI.

findings.problem: A rejected result could previously omit explicit prohibitions for the retry.
findings.evidence: The historical review format permits an empty forbidNext array and the operator did not enforce decision-specific readiness.
findings.correction: Require at least one forbid-next rule for REJECTED and provide live UI guidance.

findings.problem: The historical candidate review has no reviewer identity or timestamp.
findings.evidence: reviewer and reviewedAt are null.
findings.correction: Keep lightweight candidate reviews non-authoritative; require named reviewer and timestamp for HUMAN_SELECTED only.

findings.problem: Art-direction conformity was marked PASS despite visible material, repair-story and priority failures.
findings.evidence: The image shows generic distress, mineral-like panels and toy-defense dominance while review.json marks artDirectionConformity PASS.
findings.correction: Use the specific Salvaged Frontier assessment label and allow acceptance only after all concrete art-direction cues pass.

findings.problem: The historical review promotes the whole 2x2 sheet without identifying which candidate should survive.
findings.evidence: No selected region, quadrant identifier or crop binding exists in result.json or review.json.
findings.correction: Do not promote this sheet; use it only as historical exploration evidence and start v2 from the closed canon.

acceptanceForNextGeneration: Exactly one object construction and one gameplay state appear across all four quadrants.
Hero front, compatible rear, matching black silhouette and elevated mobile view are present.
Three panels, two feet, frame, brace, joints, material assignment, wear and asymmetry remain identical across views.
Threat-facing front has no mint interaction cue; protected rear repair socket is visible only on the player-safe side.
The single copper repair brace connects plausible structural joints and explains one causal weak span.
Reclaimed panels read as manufactured composite, not stone, concrete, parchment or ceramic.
Salvaged Frontier identity is carried by bounded repair and replacement history while Toy Defense supplies readability only.
No emblem, pseudo-logo, generated text, uniform distress, decorative brace or invented mechanism is present.
All five review dimensions are PASS and at least one preserve rule is recorded.
gpt-image-2 use is explicitly confirmed at import.
